applicability_conditions: The test medium is aqueous and contains available iron(III).
The phenolic hydroxy group is structurally accessible.
The observed colour is distinct from the iron(III) reagent blank.
rule.claim: In aqueous media where iron(III) remains available for coordination, an accessible phenolic hydroxy group can form a visibly colored iron(III)-phenol or iron(III)-phenolate complex.
exclusions: This forward rule is not an unconditional colour-implies-phenol inverse.
A negative result does not exclude every phenol.
Precipitation, incompatible pH, or competing strong ligands are outside scope.
The rule does not identify a particular molecule.

source.locator: Nature 165 (1950) 1012, complete one-page letter; absorption and titration study of freshly prepared aqueous ferric chloride-phenol coloured complexes.

applicability_conditions: The problem statement supplies a finite and explicitly closed candidate set.
Every candidate has been audited for accessible phenolic hydroxy groups.

For every candidate lacking an accessible phenolic hydroxy group, in-scope non-phenolic iron(III)-chromogenic mechanisms and incompatible test conditions have been affirmatively ruled out from source-given structures or facts and trusted registry rules; mere failure to find an interferent is insufficient.
The problem statement itself, rather than the solver, describes the observed aqueous iron(III) response as characteristic.
rule.claim: For an explicitly closed candidate set supplied by the problem statement, after a complete candidate-structure audit and affirmative exclusion of in-scope non-phenolic iron(III)-chromogenic mechanisms and incompatible test conditions, a response that the problem statement itself describes as characteristic may be used only as a bounded discriminating cue to retain candidates with an accessible phenolic hydroxy group.
exclusions: This policy is not a universal colour-implies-phenol chemical law.
It does not identify an open-world unknown.
It does not authorize inference when candidate coverage or interference exclusion is incomplete.
It does not use a negative test to exclude every phenol.
The cited study reports selectivity only for its tested paint-and-resin panel and protocol; it does not itself establish this policy for arbitrary candidate domains.

source.locator: Journal of the Japan Society of Colour Material 35(2) (1962) 59-61; page 59 abstract and page 61 discussion and conclusion, limited to the tested paint-and-resin panel and protocol.

applicability_conditions: The reported cold-condition transformation is the claimed scope.
rule.claim: Under the reported cold potassium-permanganate conditions, hexamethylbenzene can be oxidized to mellitic acid.
exclusions: The record does not establish an acidic medium.
It does not generalize to arbitrary alkylbenzenes.
It does not claim a unique product, rate, or yield outside the reported protocol.

source.locator: Bulletin de la Société minéralogique de France 4 (1881) 26-28, page 26 opening paragraph.

applicability_conditions: The phase has been independently established as crystalline mellite.
The material is treated as an ideal stoichiometric phase.
rule.claim: The ideal crystalline mineral mellite has composition Al2[C6(COO)6]·16H2O, equivalently [Al(H2O)6]2·C12O12·4H2O.
exclusions: Occurrence in a coal or lignite deposit alone does not identify a sample.
Impure or nonstoichiometric material is outside scope.
This rule does not determine a thermal-decomposition residue.

source.locator: Acta Crystallographica B29 (1973) 26-31, page 26 abstract and reported single-crystal composition.

applicability_conditions: The dehydrating reagent and heating protocol are the reported benzoyl-chloride procedure.
rule.claim: In the reported six-hour heating protocol with a large excess of benzoyl chloride, mellitic acid undergoes complete dehydration to C12O9; warm-water hydration by three water equivalents regenerates the acid.
exclusions: This record does not authorize substitution of phosphorus pentoxide.
It does not generalize to arbitrary polycarboxylic acids or dehydrating reagents.

source.locator: Berichte der deutschen chemischen Gesellschaft 46 (1913) 813-815; page 814 preparation and page 815 hydration and analysis.
